verdict.rationale: Steel ships first-party agent-facing tooling: a steel-browser skill so an agent can control a browser, MCP exposure to any MCP client, and computer-use integrations. A user can therefore drive Steel through natural-language prompts given to an AI agent. However, Steel has no natural-language command interface of its own; the language understanding comes from the external agent. Missing for 10: a native natural-language command surface in Steel itself, and hands-on or independent evidence of natural-language operation working end to end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Install Steel CLI and the steel-browser skill so your agent can control a browser.
Expose a Steel browser to any MCP client
The Steel integration exposes a cloud browser as in-process MCP tools, so the SDK runs the agent loop and Steel handles the browser.
The OpenAI Computer Use integration runs OpenAI's vision-based agent loop on a Steel browser session.
